articles.title: 挑战杜比全景声：IAMF 2.0 发布，免版税的沉浸式音频新标准
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，开放媒体联盟（AOMedia）昨日（11 月 25 日）发布沉浸式音频标准 IAMF 2.0，重点新增“基于对象的音频”等能力，推进开放、免版税的沉浸式音频标准，为行业提供杜比全景声之外的另一种选择。定位方面，杜比全景声（Dolby Atmos）目前是最成熟的沉浸式音频生态之一，覆盖内容制作、流媒体平台、影院、电视、手机、耳机和游戏等多个环节。IAMF 则由 AOMedia 推动发布，强调开放、互操作和免版税，目标是让不同厂商、平台和设备更容易实现沉浸式音频。升级方面，IAMF 2.0 主要新增“基于对象的音频”能力。IAMF 此前已支持基于声道和基于场景的音频表达方式，而新版本在此基础上，允许每一个声音元素携带自身在三维空间中的位置信息。这意味着创作者不再必须把声音固定分配给某个扬声器声道，而可以更精确地安排人声、音乐、环境音和特效在空间中的位置，让听众获得更接近真实场景的沉浸感。播放设备也可根据耳机、回音壁、家庭影院或多声道扬声器等不同条件，动态调整声音呈现方式。新标准还增加了更多配置文件，并支持更复杂的扬声器布局，以覆盖高级家庭影院和专业音频制作需求。在兼容性方面，IAMF 2.0 支持 Opus、AAC-LC、FLAC 和 LPCM 四种音频编解码器，开发者可依据内容类型、带宽、延迟和音质需求选择合适的编码方案。由于 IAMF 本身独立于底层编码技术，它为不同平台和设备之间的沉浸式音频互操作提供了更灵活的基础。AOMedia 同时将 2026 年 7 月发布的 Open Audio Renderer 1.0 正式纳入 IAMF 2.0。IT之家援引博文介绍，Open Audio Renderer 则负责把这些音频数据转换成适合用户实际设备播放的信号。该渲染器已在 GitHub 上以开源形式提供，开发者可以据此构建自己的播放、渲染和分发方案。在开发工具层面，AOMedia 更新了 libiamf 参考实现，并推出可将符合音频定义模型（ADM）的源文件转换为 IAMF 流的工具。这降低了内容制作方和软件开发者接入新标准的门槛，有助于推动沉浸式音频在多媒体播放器、流媒体服务、游戏引擎、广播系统和虚拟现实应用中的落地。

articles.title: Remedy 回应玩家请求开发《量子破碎 2》：最终决定权在微软
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，微软曾与游戏开发商 Remedy 展开过广泛合作，共同开发《心灵杀手》《量子破碎》等游戏。IT之家了解到，《量子破碎》是一款以时间操纵为核心玩法的射击游戏，也是最早尝试 Xbox Play Anywhere 功能的游戏之一。它在多个方面都走在了时代前面，大胆采用了如今许多开发商正在追逐的跨媒体叙事模式，将游戏与影视内容结合起来，游戏中还出现大量 Windows Phone 广告。这款游戏 2016 年推出后，许多玩家都期待着续作，他们多年以来一直请求 Remedy 开发《量子破碎 2》。Remedy 近日（11 月 23 日）对此回应称：“据我们所知，目前还没有相关消息 😅。《量子破碎》是否推出续作由微软决定。不过看到玩家们多年来对这款游戏保持热爱，我们很高兴。”

articles.title: 商务部等 8 部门：推动优质网络文学、动漫游戏等出口，引进境外优秀视听节目和影片
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，商务部等 8 部门今日宣布印发《服务贸易发展“十五五”规划》，目标到 2030 年，服务贸易发展实现贸易规模稳步扩大，占外贸总额的比重进一步提升，服务贸易大国地位进一步稳固，服务贸易在贸易高质量发展中的作用更加突出。目标到 2035 年，全面形成服务贸易高质量发展格局，创新能力和开放水平大幅提升，我国服务贸易发展规模和国际竞争力稳居全球前列，对建成贸易强国和社会主义现代化建设的战略支撑和综合贡献进一步增强。IT之家注意到，规划文件提到，“十四五”时期，我国服务贸易有效应对一系列重大风险挑战，创新发展取得重大成就：贸易规模迈上新台阶，服务进出口总额首次突破 8 万亿元，2025 年达到 80823.1 亿元，其中出口 36267.9 亿元，年均增长 13.4%，进口 44555.1 亿元，年均增长 11.1%。行业领域呈现新发展，知识密集型服务出口占服务出口总额的比重达 50.5%，电信计算机和信息服务、知识产权使用费、其他商业服务引领增长，数字文化产品加速出海。改革创新取得新突破，全面深化服务贸易创新发展试点成效显著，特色服务出口基地成为出口重要支点，服务外包示范城市引领产业转型升级。对外开放迈出新步伐，建立跨境服务贸易负面清单管理制度和梯度开放体系，高质量实施《区域全面经济伙伴关系协定》，推动世界贸易组织成员达成服务贸易国内规制参考文件、投资便利化协定和电子商务协定。综合贡献实现新提升，服务贸易占外贸比重提升至 15.1%，成为增长新引擎，为我国参与全球价值链分工、提升产业竞争力和扩大服务消费供给发挥了积极作用。规划文件要求提升“制造 + 服务”综合竞争力。发挥“中国制造”优势，推动服务贸易与高端制造业融合发展，在生物医药、集成电路、飞机、汽车、工程机械、高铁、船舶等领域培育一批综合服务提供商，形成重点服务产业链或产业集群。引导生产性服务业与制造业协同出海，服务产供链合理有序跨境布局。拓展综合保税区功能，优化保税监管制度，扩大研发、设计、检测、维修、供应链物流等生产性服务出口。发展“数字孪生 + 智能制造”“工业互联网 + 供应链”等新业态。推动互联网平台型企业提供跨境供应链、数字营销、数据分析等一站式服务，助力中小制造企业与全球采购商高效对接。规划文件支持金融保险服务出口。做好金融服务产业链供应链合理有序跨境布局，提升人民币金融服务全球竞争力。鼓励金融机构采取差异化、多样化战略，为企业贸易投资合作提供契合实际、符合需要的金融服务。借助大数据、区块链等金融科技，将金融服务嵌入智能制造、智能物流、智能仓储等各个环节，培育金融服务贸易竞争新优势。拓宽人民币跨境支付系统（CIPS）网络广度和深度，提升系统功能和服务。规划文件还提到，更好发挥国家文化出口重点企业和项目引领作用，扩大出版物出口和版权贸易，推动优质网络文学、视听节目、动漫游戏、数字电影、演艺服务、文化艺术品等出口。规划文件要求修订发布《鼓励进口服务目录》。服务新质生产力发展和绿色低碳转型需要，扩大研发设计、资源循环利用、环境治理等生产性服务进口。满足人民群众对高品质生活的需求，鼓励医疗健康、演出赛事等更多优质生活性服务进口，引进境外优秀视听节目和影片，办好国际电影节、电视节，做好涉外影视节展工作，扩大多元化服务供给。

articles.title: 《GTA 6》民间 PC 移植新突破：已能渲染游戏世界，帧率约 5~7 FPS
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，科技媒体 tweaktown 昨日（11 月 25 日）发布博文，报道称开源社区借助 AI 以及此前曝光的 XBOX 可执行文件，正在加速推进非官方 PC 移植《侠盗猎车手 VI》（GTA 6）游戏。名为“Belobug”的项目近日宣布，已能在 Windows 11 电脑上启动并渲染《GTA 6》的开放世界，画面包含光照、纹理、行人、车辆、植被、水体和天空等要素，运行帧率约为每秒 5 至 7 帧。IT之家注：Belobug 是另一款移植项目“Victory”的分支，以泄露的 XBOX 内部构建文件为“蓝图”，将相关文件交由 Claude 和 Gemini Antigravity 等人工智能工具解析、重组，并协助生成可用于 PC 平台的代码。项目开发者称，该版本在配备 AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16GB 显卡、Ryzen 7 9800X3D 处理器和 64GB 内存的电脑上测试，游戏完成度已达到 77.4%。目前，项目尚未在 Nvidia 或 Intel 显卡上进行测试。

articles.title: OpenAI 开始合并 ChatGPT 聊天 / 工作模式，重度用户可能更早触及限额
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，OpenAICodex&ChatGPT 团队负责人蒂博 · 索蒂奥（Tibo）今天宣布，公司已开始向小部分 Pro 订阅用户推送 ChatGPT 聊天 / 工作模式合并。部分用户对此表示批评，担心此举可能会限制他们的使用额度。OpenAI 发言人向科技媒体 TechCrunch 表示，大多数用户预计不会因此更频繁地遇到使用额度重置。但少数用量较高的重度用户可能会更早触及额度上限。同时，虽然聊天 / 工作模式将共享额度系统。但使用 Instant 模型进行的对话将不计入用量，即使用户已经耗尽使用额度，仍然可以继续使用 Instant 模型。OpenAI 将于 12 月进一步扩大额度共享的覆盖范围。

articles.title: 鸿蒙智行问界新 M7 车型开启预售，30.98 万元起
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，鸿蒙智行问界新 M7 车型今日官宣开启预售，预售价 30.98 万元起。即刻预订，可享 2000 元意向金抵 5000 元购车尾款权益。首批展车已陆续到店。作为年度改款，新车外观轮廓与在售车型基本一致，核心升级集中在智能驾驶硬件架构、座舱交互与动力电池三个维度。官方将其定位为“幸福旗舰”，面向家庭出行场景，五座与六座布局均继续提供。其车身尺寸维持 5080×1999×1780mm，轴距 3030mm，定位于中大型 SUV。外观新增翡冷翠与暖阳金两款车色，增程版与纯电版在前格栅造型上有所区分。智驾方面，问界新 M7 升级了面向 L3 级自动驾驶的全域冗余架构，并搭载华为乾崑智驾 ADS 5 系统。硬件层面，C 柱新增一颗摄像头以补强侧后方感知，翼子板处增加补盲激光雷达，顶配车型的激光雷达数量可能进一步增加。座舱方面，新车中控台整体加宽加厚，副驾驶前方换装一块大尺寸屏幕，替代现款相对小巧的副驾屏。内饰采用双拼配色，门板加入山影刺绣纹样，座椅使用菱形绗缝工艺，整体氛围向精致与东方美学靠拢。动力延续增程与纯电双线。增程版搭载 1.5T 增程器，发动机最大功率 118kW，前、后电机最大功率分别为 170kW 与 227kW；纯电版前、后电机分别为 160kW 与 227kW。增程版电池容量有望提升至 56 度，纯电续航进一步延长；纯电版预计继续搭载约 100 度三元锂电池，CLTC 续航最远可超 700 公里。全系基于 800V 高压架构，支持超快充补能。

articles.title: 我国科研团队从地衣真菌中发现作物抗旱增产新基因：单株产量最多提高 42.4%，成果登上 Nature
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，西北农林科技大学今日宣布，11 月 25 日，该校康振生院士 / 毛虎德研究员团队联合中国科学院微生物研究所魏江春院士团队，在国际顶级学术期刊《自然》（Nature）在线发表了题为《嗜极生物来源基因提升禾谷类作物抗旱性与产量》的研究论文。该研究突破利用作物自身遗传资源开展抗逆改良的传统范式，从长期适应极端干旱生境的地衣真菌中挖掘新型抗旱基因，为打破作物抗旱与产量之间的权衡，培育抗旱高产粮食作物，提供了新的遗传资源与理论思路。长期以来，作物育种领域存在一大难题：作物抗旱能力提升的同时往往伴随产量下降，而高产品种又普遍耐旱性偏弱，抗旱与高产之间难以兼顾，这也成为旱区作物遗传改良亟待突破的关键卡点。团队将研究视角投向能够在极端环境存活的地衣。地衣是由真菌和光合共生生物形成的特殊共生体系，可以在干旱、贫瘠、高寒等严酷环境中长期生存，蕴含着独特的抗逆基因资源。通过大规模筛选，团队从地衣型真菌石果衣基因组中鉴定出新的抗逆基因 EpTFIIAγ，经过跨物种遗传转化以及多年份、多地点、多遗传背景的田间试验证明，该基因能够精准协调植物逆境生存与生长发育的动态平衡，显著提高小麦、水稻、玉米等粮食作物的抗旱能力，且在干旱环境下单株产量提高 19.7%—42.4%，正常供水条件下仍能促进部分作物产量提升。研究证实，遭遇干旱时，该基因帮助作物改善水分利用效率、延缓植株衰老，显著增强耐旱能力；水分供给充足时，该基因能够提升作物光合碳同化效率，优化“源 — 库”关系，充分保障作物的产量潜力，以此巧妙化解抗旱与产量此消彼长的冲突。团队还进一步解析了该基因独特的分子作用机制，发现蛋白 N 端特殊的内在无序区是发挥功能的关键。依托该区域，通过 DNA 结合初步定位、内源转录因子靶向识别、多价互作增效的多层级调控模式，整合到植物内源转录调控网络中，协同调控逆境响应、生长发育和产量形成相关通路，最终实现抗旱性与产量同步提升。同时，该研究拓展了转录因子依赖单一结构域精准识别靶基因的传统认知，为转录调控“涌现特异性”理论提供了重要实验佐证，揭示了外源基因嵌入并重塑作物内源调控网络的全新分子机制。IT之家附论文链接：https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11151-w

articles.title: Co-World Model for Human-Video-to-Robot Transfer via Co-Constructed Shared Latent Dynamics
articles.content: Human videos are abundant and cheap to obtain, whereas robot trajectories remain scarce and costly, making zero-shot skill transfer from a single human demonstration an appealing route to scalable robot learning. Existing methods, however, either retarget human-specific geometry or match only static visual goals, and thus stumble over the cross-embodiment dynamics mismatch and the ungrounded action execution. We present the Co-World Model (CoWM), a predictive framework jointly optimized from paired yet unsynchronized human and robot streams. To bridge the cross-embodiment dynamics gap, CoWM disentangles each observation into a shared object-relation state and embodiment-specific context. It aligns latent actions across embodiments using effect-swap and action-sensitivity objectives,such that actions are matched by their predicted effects on the manipulated objects rather than by embodimentdependent kinematics. For grounded execution, a phase-aware receding-horizon controller estimates demonstration progress, projects the inferred human action prior onto the robot action-support density, and translates the resulting latent dynamics into executable robot commands. Extensive experiments in simulation and on two physical robot platforms demonstrate the effectiveness of CoWM, its cross-platform generalizability, and the contribution of each component. See the demo video in the supporting information for details.

articles.title: RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations
articles.content: Random projection is a basic compression primitive for Euclidean representation learning, with the Johnson--Lindenstrauss lemma giving a target dimension $k=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n)$ independent of the ambient dimension. As hyperbolic representations gain increasing attention in modern Transformers, vision-language models, and large language models, the same need for oblivious dimensionality reduction arises, but no analogous primitive yet exists for hyperbolic representations. We study this gap. Two natural attempts fail in dual ways: a tangent-space scheme gives a clean local guarantee but is chart-bound and pays a curvature penalty, while a fully hyperbolic projection in the hyperboloid model is geometrically native but mixes radial and angular error before feeding them into the conditioning of $\operatorname{arcosh}$. We propose radial-angular random projection (RAP), which preserves the radial coordinate exactly and applies a Euclidean random projection only to the angular direction, lifting the result back to the target hyperboloid. RAP is hyperbolic-to-hyperbolic by construction, costs one Gaussian matrix-vector product, and reduces hyperbolic compression to a normalized angular JL question on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. We prove a finite-set RAP guarantee with explicit $\sinh(\sqrt{c}\,r_x)\sinh(\sqrt{c}\,r_y)$ conditioning, complemented by a local tangent-space JL theorem and an arcosh-conditioning lemma for the fully hyperbolic comparator. Across an origin-centered broad-radius point cloud, a balanced tree, a clustered Gaussian, and the WordNet noun hierarchy, RAP attains the lowest mean relative distortion in every $(n,k)$ cell, reducing distortion over the strongest hyperbolic baseline by approximately $48\%$--$49\%$ on broad-radius data. RAP also scales to million-point datasets and improves retrieval on vision--language representations over hyperbolic projection baselines.

articles.title: BOT-Scale: A Traceable Evaluation Methodology for Robotic Manipulation
articles.content: A successful manipulation rollout can still involve a mid-task object drop or a placement deviation. Existing evaluators reduce such deviations to a single score or attach explanations computed separately; the score itself explains neither its basis nor what to fix. We show that a manipulation score becomes traceable when defined as the sum of outcome-conditioned penalties over retained behavioral-factor records. Explanation and score share the same computation, so each factor-level deduction names an inspectable deviation. BOT-Scale applies this principle by adapting behavioral assessment scales from medicine. It organizes twelve candidate factors into four assessment layers; each factor is tied to observable evidence and an explicit decision criterion. Reference calibration fixes a penalty per factor, and a closed-form rule aggregates the factor records into a score with per-factor contributions. We developed BOTScorer, an automatic scoring system based on the seven factors retained by data-driven screening, to validate this methodology. We provide BOT-Events, a dataset with eight-rater quality scores and factor-event annotations, alongside the traceable, interpretable score. The code will be released publicly.

articles.title: LatENSO v1.0: a learned latent state of the tropical Pacific for seasonal ENSO operators and forecasting
articles.content: Here we present LatENSO v1.0, a machine-learning forecast system for the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) built around a learned, 32-dimensional state of the tropical Pacific. A Swin-transformer autoencoder compresses thirteen monthly-averaged ocean and atmosphere fields into 32 numbers, trained to reconstruct the fields, with no forecast target. The 32 numbers rebuild the fields as well as O(100) empirical orthogonal functions. Two seasonal operators use this state. The first is the extended nonlinear recharge oscillator (XRO) with two directions of the learned state among its variables; we call it XRO-lat. The second is a Floquet modal operator (FMO) of three damped oscillators, which forecasts a correction added to a least-squares base forecast made from four observed predictors. We evaluate both against the recharge oscillator, XRO and a deep echo-state network (DESN), all refitted on identical data, cross-validation folds and verification windows (1981-2024). Over lead times of 1-18 months, XRO-lat reaches an anomaly correlation coefficient (ACC) of 0.673, the highest of all tropical-Pacific-only (in-domain) systems and statistically indistinguishable from XRO and DESN with their eight remote-basin indices (0.685 and 0.667). From lead 15 to lead 24 it is the most skillful of all systems. Over leads 1-18, the FMO forecast (0.619) is statistically indistinguishable from every in-domain reference model (0.631-0.654). What the FMO adds to its base forecast, 0.054 in ACC, is carried by its Floquet propagation, whose generator consistently holds a prominent quasi-biennial oscillator. At leads 3-9 the FMO trails XRO, DESN and the in-domain XRO, a deficit partly attributable to its base. LatENSO combines competitive skill with trustworthiness: a compact state whose physical content can be inspected, and fully open access to code, weights and data.

articles.title: WebVibe: Multimodal Interactive Website Generation via Reverse Synthesis and Visual Self-Distillation
articles.content: Although multimodal large language models translate single screenshots into static HTML, generating interactive functional websites from design specifications still struggles with multi-page routing and stateful widget transitions. Examining existing training pipelines reveals two bottlenecks: (1) in forward data synthesis (X -> Y), writing the specification X before code execution leaves unimplemented or altered requirements in X as supervision noise; and (2) in reinforcement learning, scalar rewards discard the rich state transitions observed during replay. Based on these findings, we introduce WebVibe and Interactive-SDPO to train InteractiveCoder. WebVibe reverses synthesis into Y -> X by verifying cross-page and in-page interactions in the browser before deriving multimodal inputs from replay-confirmed states to build the 31,542-site WebVibe-32K corpus with reusable execution contracts. Interactive-SDPO then conditions a weight-sharing self-teacher on the replay trace and a 2x2 state-transition montage to provide token-level supervision at zero inference-time overhead. On the public Vision2Web L2, one-shot InteractiveCoder-9B nearly 3x its base model's functional score (20.2 to 55.2 FS) and matches a 1T-parameter coding agent in a single pass with 111x fewer total parameters and 78x fewer tokens. On our WebVibeBench, InteractiveCoder-4B and 9B further outperform all evaluated baselines by over 23 points.

articles.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
articles.content: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. Active States translate state discrepancies identified during review into concrete visual asset requirements that guide reference construction, validation, and regeneration, preserving identity and already-correct content while repairing target attributes. Confirmed generation results are linked to the corresponding asset states, story time, and reference versions for verification and reuse by subsequent shots. Hierarchical Collaboration isolates execution contexts by task, clip, and repair round, and uses hierarchical memory to organize this process across multiple sets. Across multiple benchmarks, StateWeaver outperforms existing methods and produces long videos with sustained cross-shot consistency under predefined and autonomously planned storyboards.

articles.title: Rehearse in 3D, Render in 2D: Physically Consistent and Editable Robot World Models
articles.content: Embodied world models aim to predict future interactions that are both visually realistic and physically consistent. Yet explicit 3D motion prediction alone does not guarantee that object structure and contact relationships are preserved. Beyond motion prediction, 3D representations provide an explicit state space for imposing structural and physical constraints. Building on this insight, we introduce RehearsalWorld, an editable robot world model driven by 3D Interaction Rehearsal (3DIR). Given an initial RGB-D observation and robot actions, Interaction-Consistent Rehearsal (ICR) uses a pretrained 3D point-flow model as a motion prior. It refines the predicted trajectories through response-aware object grouping, persistent grasp memory, and contact structure refiner, preserving scene stability, object structure, and grasp attachments. Rehearsal-Aligned Video Generation (RAVG) then uses geometric projections of the rehearsal as temporal conditioning. We fine-tune a video generator on projection-video pairs to synthesize realistic interaction videos. Thanks to the decoupling of physical response from visual synthesis, RehearsalWorld also supports independent editing of material properties and camera viewpoints. Compared with PointWorld on real DROID grasping sequences, RehearsalWorld reduces gripper-relative offset by approximately 79% to 84% across deformable, articulated, and rigid objects and lowers reference motion error. For video prediction, it achieves a PSNR of 23.92 dB and an FVD of 149.

articles.content: We present a dataset of 340 fully synthetic manipulation demonstrations generated from real seed data for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) training. The corpus contains 32,340 frames with synchronized RGB and actions across eight object categories, represented as LeRobot v2.1 episodes with H.264 video, per-frame robot states and pose-valued action labels, language task annotations, summary statistics and quality decisions. Each synthetic demonstration is produced without additional teleoperation: a LoRA-fine-tuned Cosmos-3 model generates a manipulation video, and RoboHaMeR recovers the corresponding robot trajectory from RGB. Quality screening accepted 300 of 340 episodes for policy fine-tuning. As preliminary evidence of feasibility, a pretrained GR00T N1.6 policy fine-tuned exclusively on the 300 accepted episodes reaches 16/20 (80%) real-world pick-and-place success on the Oreo-package task. A policy fine-tuned on 105 real teleoperated episodes achieved 18/20 (90%) under the same protocol. These results are based on one object and 20 trials per policy and are therefore reported as preliminary evidence rather than a general performance claim.

articles.title: ReMeDi: Single-Image PBR Material Estimation via Reparameterization between Metal and Dielectric Hypotheses
articles.content: Physically based rendering (PBR) material estimation facilitates relighting, material editing, and 3D content creation. As the reflectance of a surface heavily depends on whether it is a metal or a dielectric, producing any map that determines albedo involves a decision on metalness, which we call the "intended metalness" of the map. Rendering maps with mismatched intended metalness yields physically implausible or misinterpreted materials. The metallic--roughness workflow makes metalness explicit and thus encourages base color to match it, but does not enforce this match, especially for automated methods directly predicting each map. Therefore, we propose ReMeDi, which enforces the match through two components. First, we reparameterize base color as a metalness-weighted blend of its two variants, estimated under the all-metal and all-dielectric hypothesis, respectively. Second, as available supervision cannot teach a single network both hypotheses at every pixel, we restrict each of two separate networks to one hypothesis, so that each variant is ensured to follow its hypothesis. Besides enforcing the match, this also improves each estimated material map. Experiments show that ReMeDi outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both material accuracy and relighting fidelity.

articles.title: Escapingthe instruction blackhole of vision-language-action policies via optimal-transport wormholes
articles.content: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are trained to follow a fixed instruction, yet people change their minds while the robot acts. We identify the instruction black hole: once a VLA policy commits to a task, new instructions are absorbed and the robot completes the old task or freezes. We quantify it with a transmission ratio and an event horizon and prove it is a blind spot of static imitation, which cannot distinguish a policy that listens from a deaf one once the execution state reveals the task. We propose Wormhole, a training-free plug-in that relocates the robot instead of re-instructing it: optimal transport selects an approach-phase state of the new task, a rate-limited traversal carries the robot there, and the unmodified policy takes over. On LIBERO,Wormhole raises committed-switch success of pi to and pi0.5 from at most 1.2% to 93.1%, matching or exceeding scripted retreat-and-restart with one fifth of its action discontinuity.

articles.title: Semantic State Reading for Joint Image-Semantic Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Pretrained visual representations improve diffusion-transformer training, yet exploiting both global context and local spatial structure requires deciding which semantic states to model and how to access them. We introduce Semantic State Reading (SSR), which jointly denoises image latents, a global CLS token encoding image-level context, and a compact patch state preserving spatial correspondence. SSR couples this global-local modeling with distinct reading paths: local states are fused with corresponding image tokens at the input, while independent projections inject the current global state into every transformer block. Both semantic scopes thus remain accessible throughout denoising. Ablations show complementary benefits from local-state modeling and repeated global reading, and semantic-trajectory interventions alter image layout under a fixed class label. On ImageNet $256 \times 256$, SiT-XL/2 with SSR reaches or surpasses the reference FIDs of SiT, REPA, and Representation Entanglement for Generation (REG) with $100\times$, $40\times$, and $2\times$ fewer training iterations, respectively. SSR achieves unguided FID 1.78 at 2M iterations and FID 1.34 with classifier-free guidance alone. Combining classifier-free guidance with autoguidance yields FID 1.31 at 1M iterations, achieving the best FID in our main comparison table.

articles.title: Latent-in-the-Middle: On the Security of Cross-Model Latent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
articles.content: As large language models increasingly collaborate in heterogeneous multi-agent systems, latent communication has emerged as an efficient alternative to exchanging natural-language messages. By sharing internal representations, agents can avoid repeatedly processing the same context, reducing communication overhead and prefill computation. One such mechanism is cross-model Key-Value (KV) cache transfer, which uses a learned mapper to translate a source model's KV cache into one a target model can use. However, this handoff means the target model consumes context it did not encode itself, thus calling into question whether its safety alignment still holds.   In this work, we investigate the security implications of latent handoffs by introducing Chasm, a framework characterizing cross-model handoff attacks across three new attack surfaces: the source model, mapper, and handoff mechanism itself. Our experiments reveal that latent handoffs substantially undermine safety alignment and prompt-injection defenses. Notably, a target model that follows only 0.4% of benchmark prompt injections natively, follows up to 44.2% when transferred through a mapper from a source model. On the other hand, for jailbreak attacks, transfer alone raises attack success by up to 24.6 pp within a model family and zero-shot attacks by up to 69.2 pp, whereas white-box optimization through the mapper boosts the attack success rate to 92.5%, against 37.5% for ordinary GCG on the same target. To address these vulnerabilities, we propose a lightweight target-side cache guard that corrects transferred caches to restore the target model's refusal, considerably mitigating these attacks.

articles.title: Beat This! Live - Online Beat and Downbeat Tracking by Predicting the Future
articles.content: Beat and downbeat tracking have seen multiple improvements through recent deep learning approaches, but most target an offline setting, precluding their use in real-time scenarios. We adapt a recent offline beat tracking model, Beat This, for online, low-latency operation and propose Beat This! Live, a causal variant designed for real-time beat and downbeat tracking. We present the architectural modifications required to obtain a causal system suitable for streaming inference and measure their impact on accuracy. By training our model with temporally shifted labels, it produces predictions slightly ahead of the current frame, which not only reduces latency, but enables much more effective peak-picking. Evaluation on the GTZAN dataset shows the F1-score improves from 80.6 to 86.7 for beats and 56.5 to 74.1 for downbeats compared to BeatNet+, the current state of the art in online beat tracking.

articles.title: Scaling Looped MoE Language Models under Matched Budgets: Information Flow and Parameter Allocation
articles.content: Looped Transformers decouple computational depth from parameter count, and prior studies have demonstrated promising performance gains with increased computation. However, systematic design principles for configuring these models under strict iso-parameter and iso-FLOP constraints remain scarce. We contribute to this direction by improving information flow in looped models and systematically studying loop parameter configurations. Specifically, we refine this information flow via gated inner-loop state updates and a cross-stage residual connection. Building on this design, controlled studies identify a configuration combining a single-pass Core depth of 25%-35% of the total unrolled depth with reallocating saved parameters into extra routed experts per layer, improving performance at zero extra compute while preserving compatibility with existing training infrastructure. Evaluated after 1T pre-training tokens, our 69B MLA and 51B KDA Mixture-of-Experts models outperform budget-matched non-recurrent baselines by an average of 1.16 and 2.29 percentage points across four benchmarks, respectively. Further reproduction experiments on a common backbone with a 200B-token training budget show that our method achieves lower perplexity than other looped methods. Code for these reproduction experiments is available at https://github.com/lxi01766/Scaling-Looped-MoE-Language-Models-under-Matched-Budgets-Information-Flow-and-Parameter-Allocation.

articles.title: LatentCP-DPO: Conformal Pessimism for DPO with Finite-Sample Guarantees
articles.content: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) learns a response policy from human preference data, but with a limited dataset it can overfit to noisy or weakly informative preference labels. We introduce LatentCP-DPO, a framework that combines conformal prediction with pessimistic preference optimization for Bradley-Terry (BT) pairwise feedback and Plackett-Luce (PL) ranking feedback. Building on LatentCP's construction of uncertainty sets for unobserved model parameters, we address how to incorporate this uncertainty into preference optimization and characterize its effect on policy performance. Under exchangeability and a correctly specified preference model, we construct uncertainty sets for latent relative rewards with finite-sample marginal coverage from conformal prediction sets for observable preferences. We then learn a response policy by maximizing the worst-case expected preference log-likelihood over these uncertainty sets, using an independent collection of prompts and candidate responses without preference labels. Under suitable assumptions, we establish finite-sample upper bounds on regularized policy suboptimality that separate policy-class approximation error, conformal uncertainty, and statistical estimation error. For BT feedback, we further establish a worst-case lower bound for LatentCP-DPO that matches the upper bound's reciprocal dependence on the number of unlabeled optimization examples. The lower bound also shows that the uncertainty sets can induce a bias that persists as the optimization sample grows. Together, these results characterize both the statistical accuracy and potential limitations of preference optimization using conformal uncertainty sets. Experiments support the benefits of the proposed framework in finite preference datasets.

articles.title: Libtt: A Compiler and Runtime for Tenstorrent Processors
articles.content: Libtt brings the PyTorch and JAX ecosystem to Tenstorrent hardware. It implements PJRT, the interface through which XLA-based frameworks drive Google's TPUs, so JAX runs on it directly, PyTorch runs through TorchTPU, and software written for TPUs carries over with no changes except replacing custom kernels. Built on Tenstorrent's open-source compiler and runtime, libtt ships the entire stack, from the compiler to the multi-chip runtime, as a single shared library. It contains extensive fixes to the upstream Tenstorrent software to make existing PyTorch and JAX code work out of the box, and extensive new compiler optimizations to make it fast. It passes most of the JAX and TorchTPU test suites and runs SGLang, TorchTitan, and Miles, covering serving, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.

articles.title: LLM-coupled interpretable tool wear monitoring with multi-evidence reasoning in CNC machining
articles.content: Interpretable tool wear assessment in CNC machining is challenging. Existing diagnostic models have high accuracy but provide limited guidance for tool replacement. This study proposes a two layer framework combining deep learning wear classification and LLM assisted reasoning. The first layer uses PCA Loading feature selection and optimized GRU to recognize three wear states, achieving 98.38 percent macro F1 score on the PHM2010 dataset. The second layer uses LLMs to generate natural language reports and replacement suggestions from classification results and feature trends. Engineer evaluation shows the reports outperform rule templates. Cross dataset tests on NASA milling data support the generalizability of this framework.

articles.title: TORE: Token-Wise Taylor Order Selection via Decomposed Residual Error Estimation for Diffusion Acceleration
articles.content: Diffusion models excel at image and video generation, but iterative denoising incurs substantial inference latency. Recent token-adaptive acceleration methods select Taylor prediction orders for the full-model residual using shallow-layer proxy scores. However, candidate orders are evaluated on these proxy features but used to predict the full-model residual, creating a proxy--target mismatch: the proxy-preferred order may not minimize residual prediction error. To address this mismatch, we propose \textbf{TORE} (\textbf{T}aylor \textbf{O}rder selection via \textbf{R}esidual \textbf{E}rror estimation), which selects token-wise Taylor orders based on estimated prediction errors for the full-model residual. Yet direct error evaluation requires future ground-truth residuals, which are unavailable during order selection. TORE therefore estimates prediction error by analyzing how errors arise in Taylor extrapolation. Specifically, it decomposes prediction error into truncation error and finite-difference derivative error, then estimates both contributions from cached residuals to preselect token-wise orders for upcoming skip steps. Extensive experiments show that TORE achieves $4.31\times$ speedup on FLUX.1-dev and $4.18\times$ on Wan2.1 while maintaining high generation quality and fidelity.

articles.title: Train-Only-Constrained LM for Synthetic Clinical Trajectories: Leak-Safe Calibration and Auditable Dynamics
articles.content: Simulating clinical time series necessitates temporal realism, calibration that preserves model integrity, and privacy transparency. We present a train-only, constrained language-model pipeline that factorizes generation. A compact GPT-style language model learns cross-biomarker co-occurrence through quantile tokens, and temporal directions are enforced by 3x3 per-biomarker Markov transitions fit on TRAIN, allowing dynamics to be audited. We fit a monotone quantile map (QMap) on TRAIN only (SYN(TRAIN) -> SIM(TRAIN)); no TEST statistics are used. The fixed map is then applied to SYN(TEST) severities. The constrained LM demonstrated improved distributional fidelity and co-occurrence in a 5,000-patient simulated testbed (parameters within published clinical ranges) compared to an empirical sampler, maintained near-chance detectability after a small lambda-sweep, and exhibits temporal adherence by construction. A classifier-based membership-inference audit results in an AUC of approximately 0.5; we make no differential-privacy claim. We present multi-seed results with paired 95% confidence intervals and quantify the severity of QMap's alignment (Delta W1 with confidence interval). This is a Stage-1 method result obtained on a controlled simulator; Stage-2 validation on real EHR cohorts with clinical endpoints is planned.

articles.title: CamAct: Learning Robotic Manipulation from In-the-Wild Videos via Camera Motion
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models benefit from large, diverse datasets for robotic manipulation, yet collecting robot demonstrations remains costly. Recent work has explored egocentric videos as a source of supervision, primarily drawing on demonstrations of human-object interaction. We show that in-the-wild videos can improve robotic manipulation even when they contain no demonstrations of object manipulation. Specifically, camera motion recovered from these videos provides an additional source of motion supervision that complements robot demonstrations. Building on this finding, we introduce CamAct, which incorporates this camera-motion supervision into VLA policies alongside robot demonstrations, extending the use of human videos for manipulation learning beyond object interactions. Experiments show that incorporating this video supervision during fine-tuning improves success rates from 96.40% to 98.10% on LIBERO and from 22.96% to 29.32% on RoboCasa 365. The resulting policy also demonstrates strong results in out-of-distribution generalization on LIBERO-Plus and real-world manipulation tasks.

articles.title: Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments
articles.content: Large language models (LLMs) perform well on chemistry knowledge benchmarks, which mainly assess question answering and isolated tasks. Chemical research, however, requires using specialized tools and interpreting their outputs to obtain chemically valid results. To address this gap, we introduce Crucible Bench to evaluate this ability across all four stages of the design-make-test-analyze (DMTA) cycle. The benchmark contains 1,078 tasks in 12 task families curated from 18 published datasets, covering molecular design, synthesis planning, experimental execution, closed-loop optimization, simulation, and analytical characterization. Agents access 75 domain-specific tools through the Model Context Protocol in seven isolated environments. Sandboxed graders verify the resulting synthesis routes, experimental protocols, and other outputs. Laboratory tasks use robotic simulators or previously measured experimental data. We evaluate 14 LLMs as agents and find that the best achieves an overall score of 0.545, with synthesis planning and closed-loop optimization emerging as the hardest domains. Overall performance does not predict optimization performance well: the model ranked twelfth overall achieves the highest score in closed-loop optimization. Error analysis also shows that agents often submit chemically invalid results despite running their tools successfully. Stronger models benefit more from tool access, but reliable use of chemical software remains a challenge that Crucible Bench can track as models improve.

articles.title: Detector Operating Behavior Inference via Data-Space Sampling
articles.content: A detector scores candidate detections, but the recall and false alarms at a given confidence threshold depend on the input distribution. We introduce Detector Operating Behavior Inference (DOBI), a second-level inference task: estimating a fixed detector's threshold-dependent, distribution-level operating response from the internal evidence of a single unlabeled image. DOBI treats the detector's threshold response, i.e. recall, false positives, and precision across thresholds, as a latent behavioral state under the current data condition. Controlled data-space sampling probes this state space offline, and a lightweight monitor learns the inverse map from one image to this state, whose single functional output supports multiple operating policies. In a controlled proof of concept with a fixed YOLOv10-Nano person detector and COCO-derived degradations, predicted PR behavior reduces mean absolute deviation from 0.128 for an image-independent mean-behavior prior to 0.054, and predicted functional distances track empirical regime distances (Spearman 0.96). From one unlabeled image, the inferred behavior selects operating points as well as a non-deployable lookup that knows the true regime (macro-regime $F_1$ 0.6604 for both, versus 0.6407 under pristine calibration; oracle 0.6620). On this discrete benchmark, regime-supervised curve lookups are strong controls. Pre-specified continuous and compositional probing shows where functional inference matters: on unseen combinations, the functional decoder has a lower mean curve error than a template lookup, increasingly with distance from the training conditions, whereas the lookup is more accurate for interpolation. These results establish the feasibility of single-image inference of distribution-level detector behavior over the probed conditions. Source code is available at https://github.com/beckerio/dobi

articles.title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
articles.content: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use skills to access domain knowledge and complete real-world tasks. We observe that even when a skill specifies the rules and procedures needed for a task, agents may fail to apply them effectively during autonomous execution, a phenomenon we call skill Enable But Underuse (EBU). This issue is particularly consequential in medical tasks, where overlooking a single critical constraint can yield a plausible but incorrect result. To evaluate and address EBU, we introduce MedSkill-E$^{2}$, a framework for evaluating and evolving skills for medical agents. We construct EBU-Bench, a challenging benchmark covering 12 medically relevant task groups and associated skills, to evaluate agents' ability to use available skills autonomously. We quantify the EBU gap as the difference in skill-use accuracy between autonomous use and explicitly guided reading and application of the same skill. On EBU-Bench, all evaluated model-harness combinations exhibit EBU, with a mean gap of 43.94 percentage points (pp). For the same model, skill-use accuracy under autonomous use differs by up to 38.96 pp across harnesses. Motivated by these observations, we propose EBU-Evolve, which uses execution feedback from autonomous and explicitly guided skill use to distill effective guidance into reusable skill instructions. Relative to their pre-evolution versions, the revised skills improve skill-use accuracy during autonomous execution by 33.33 to 55.17 pp and continue to yield improvements when transferred across multiple models and harnesses. Our results show that autonomous skill-use accuracy varies across harnesses with the model and skill held fixed, and model rankings can change. EBU can persist even after a skill is opened. EBU-Evolve improves autonomous skill-use accuracy on unseen tasks within the same skill, with gains transferring across models and harnesses.

articles.title: Navigent: A Geometry-Grounded Agentic Framework for Vision Language Navigation
articles.content: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) with general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offers a flexible alternative to task-specific navigation policies, while reliable long-horizon execution remains challenging. Agents must track navigation progress, detect discrepancies between commanded and actual motion, and recognize when movement has passed relevant landmarks or entrances. We present Navigent, an agentic VLN framework built around a frozen MLLM and a Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic (GEC). GEC performs two complementary checks: action-to-motion consistency, which evaluates measured displacement against commanded movement, and motion-to-landmark consistency, which tracks agent-selected visual anchors and entrance candidates in world coordinates. Detected discrepancies interrupt the remaining action sequence and trigger reobservation, local adjustment, or node-based recovery. Historical visual memory supports progress tracking across extended routes. An offline self-improvement procedure further analyzes successful and failed training trajectories to refine navigation prompts and GEC logic while keeping model weights fixed. On the R2R-CE validation-unseen split (1,839 episodes) and RxR-CE validation-unseen split(3,669 episodes), Navigent achieves 84.0%/86.0% SR and 72.9%/69.1% SPL, respectively, demonstrating the value of geometry-grounded execution verification for reliable agentic navigation. articles.title: EXPOSURE: Explaining Sources of Uncertainty in Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: Shapley values in reinforcement learning are used to explain which observation features drive an agent's behavior and expected return, but not its certainty. Explaining certainty requires understanding how observation features influence different sources of return uncertainty, and Shapley values need the agent's prediction for every subset of visible features. We propose EXPOSURE, which uses one mask-aware belief network for both action selection and Shapley explanations. It explains the variance of the return, split into an observational part due to missing features and an inherent part due to the environment's own randomness, and the entropy of its belief over the masked features. In tic-tac-toe and Minesweeper, where exact Shapley values are computable, EXPOSURE gives more accurate explanations of expected return and its uncertainty, while uniquely explaining belief uncertainty.

articles.title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
articles.content: AI systems increasingly help decide which drug targets enter costly clinical trials. We recast each target-disease hypothesis as a dated event, the pair's first clinical trial. This lets us test whether a language model can forecast such events after its training cutoff, rather than recall events before it. We rebuild a dated biomedical knowledge graph as it stood at the end of each year from 2020 up to its newest version. We then ask six open language models, with and without this graph, which targets will enter a first trial for a disease the next year. Without retrieval, the models rank about as well as trial history, a count of each target's past trials in the same therapeutic area, also after their training cutoffs. Evidence dated before the decision adds at most a small gain, before or after the models' training cutoffs. The newest graph raises five of six models clearly above that baseline, but its paths usually include the answer: the pair's own trial, dated after the decision. Evaluations of target prioritisation should date both features and labels, with evidence from before the decision and outcomes after it.

articles.title: Autonomous Vineyard Exploration using LiDAR Sensing: A Field Evaluation on Legged-Wheeled Quadruped Robot
articles.content: Autonomous navigation in vineyards presents significant challenges due to uneven terrain, sparse vegetation, and the repetitive geometric nature of vineyard rows. This paper evaluates a LiDAR-based autonomous exploration system deployed on a Unitree Go2 Wheeled quadruped robot. Our approach utilizes an iterative RANSAC-based line detection pipeline to identify vineyard rows and a finite-state navigation strategy to govern row selection and traversal. Field evaluations conducted at Denbies Vineyard (UK) demonstrate the system's ability to perform sustained autonomous row following, completing a 370m up-and-down traversal without intervention. We analyze the failure modes encountered, specifically focusing on line detection instability in sparse vegetation and the trade-offs of spatial filtering. The results suggest that, while RANSAC provides a robust geometric primitive, additional temporal filtering and adaptive perception are required for reliable lane-to-lane transitions in commercial vineyard environments. articles.content: Satellite time series capture how land surfaces change over time. Pixel-wise temporal foundation models read a year of satellite observations per pixel, yet public benchmarks lack a temporal axis or subsample it to a few dates. We introduce Analemma, a temporal benchmark of six datasets that carry every 10 and 20 m Sentinel-2 band and a time series spanning a growing season, completed where their releases omit geometry, dates, or cloud masks. One frozen-encoder protocol evaluates all models across label ratios and three seeds, with two baselines without pretraining. The TESSERA model ranks first overall. A from-scratch model on monthly composites outranks every foundation model except OlmoEarth v1.3-Base, suggesting that temporal input explains most of the performance. articles.title: VibeVideoAgent: Closing the Perceptual Loop for Code-Driven Video Generation
articles.content: Code-driven video generation asks a coding agent to write and run rendering programs. This gives exact control over typography, data visualizations, synchronized audio, and multi-shot scenes, and it leaves an editable project behind. A program that exits cleanly can still render overlapping labels, a camera aimed away from its subject, broken object interactions, or narration that drifts out of sync, and none of these raise a runtime error. Feeding rendered frames and audio back into the coding session bloats its long-horizon context, while critiquing only the finished full-resolution render turns early design mistakes into costly rewrites. We introduce VibeVideoAgent, a training-free framework that lets coding agents inspect their drafts throughout production. Multimodal perception runs in short-lived contexts kept apart from the coder and returns compact, grounded Findings. Seven primitives operate on a unified multi-clock representation of assets and drafts: they explore media from coarse to fine, verify quoted requirements with evidence from every required modality, compare a draft with a reference or an earlier revision on separate clocks, and measure stream signals locally. A lightweight staged protocol has the agent test its riskiest decision on a minimal preview first. On all 239 VibeVideoBench tasks, with matched agent runtimes and a fixed perception model, VibeVideoAgent improves holistic audiovisual quality (L3) for Claude Opus 5.5 (4.03 -> 4.43, while L2 rubric compliance rises from 98.87% to 99.35%), GPT-6 Astra (4.03 -> 4.27), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (3.97 -> 4.10), with the largest gains in audio-visual synchronization (up to +0.56). Controlled ablations show that each component contributes, and trajectory audits show that the granularity of code edits governs the trade-off between rubric adherence and perceptual quality.

articles.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
articles.content: Computer-using agents are increasingly expected to complete realistic user goals rather than isolated GUI actions. However, existing benchmarks typically isolate web, mobile, or desktop environments, leaving it unclear whether a single generalist agent can execute long-horizon workflows that span multiple operating systems and persistent application states. We introduce OS-Omni, a live cross-platform benchmark and execution environment for evaluating computer-using agents across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web environments. OS-Omni is released in versioned waves of 300 tasks each; this paper focuses on the first release, v1, which contains 48 tasks per platform and 12 cross-platform workflows that pair a desktop with an Android phone. OS-Omni provides reproducible initialization, platform-specific adapters, trajectory logging, and executable final-state evaluators, and includes controlled service-backed applications for workflows involving account, cart, budget, calendar, message, and other persistent state. Human studies show that OS-Omni tasks require 67.54 interaction steps, substantially exceeding OSWorld references of 15.0 steps. On v1, the strongest evaluated agent, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches 68.5% average success, trailing the 77.3% human reference by 8.8 points; the gap is uneven across platforms, with frontier models exceeding humans on Linux but trailing them by more than 25 points on iOS and macOS. These results indicate that current agents remain far from platform-robust, long-horizon computer use, especially when success requires sustained state tracking and durable final-state changes.

articles.title: 从 AGI 到 ASI，DeepMind 提出让 AI 自己「开公司」、重塑组织架构，自己进化
articles.content: 100 个 AI 联合做题竟学会「集体作弊」？谷歌抛出 ASI 演进新框架，揭示组织化进化的恐怖与隐忧。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       刚刚，Google DeepMind 抛出了一套从 AGI 迈向 ASI 的技术演进框架，其中有个相当大胆的设想：未来 AI 的能力增长，可能要靠它自己学会组建公司，甚至不断重写公司的组织架构。这套框架提出了 Cooperative RSI（合作式递归自我改进）机制。设想一下，成千上万个 AI Agent 可以自行分工、积累专业经验、调整协作关系，再把节省下来的算力投入新一轮研发。随着组织效率提高，系统又获得更多资源来改造自身，形成持续迭代的增长循环。这意味着，未来 AI 的进化单位可能从单个模型扩展为整个研发组织，连任务分配、专业分工和知识传递机制也会成为可优化的技术变量。不过，增加 Agent 容易，让一个组织持续创造超出资源消耗的能力增益却困难得多。Cooperative RSI 究竟怎样形成递归增长，组织效率能否像模型能力一样被规模化扩展，以及谁来判断 AI 对自身的改造确实有效？ 这些问题构成了这套框架中颇有研究空间的技术核心。01从模型扩展到组织扩展过去，AI 能力增长主要依赖模型架构、训练数据和计算规模。当多个 Agent 开始共同承担复杂研发任务时，计算资源与能力之间的关系就没有那么直接了。问题出在任务依赖和协调成本上。复杂研发通常包含大量相互依赖的环节，上游结果决定下游工作能否继续。增加 Agent 可以提高独立任务的并行吞吐，却无法直接缩短任务依赖图中的关键路径。随着成员规模扩大，中间结果传递、上下文同步和冲突解决还会消耗额外资源，组织甚至可能因为协调开销过高而降低整体效率。这使 Multi-Agent Scaling Laws 与传统模型扩展规律出现明显差异。模型扩展主要考察计算投入与性能之间的关系，而组织扩展还必须考虑通信拓扑、任务可拆分程度、成员能力差异以及知识复用效率。DeepMind 强调了数字智能区别于人类组织的几个特征：Agent 可以复制运行状态，通过高带宽通道共享知识，并在不同计算节点之间迁移工作。这些条件降低了知识传播和协作重组的成本，但复制相同模型也会带来高度相关的推理偏差。即使不同 Agent 承担不同角色，共同的知识盲区仍可能让错误在组织内部相互强化。因此，专业化需要深入到系统架构中。不同 Agent 可以维护独立的长期记忆、专用工具、领域知识和验证流程，使特定类型的工作逐渐形成可复用的执行能力。随着经验积累，部分重复推理可以转化为程序调用，原本反复生成的中间结果也能够被稳定继承。雷峰网这种变化产生了两种不同的扩展收益。并行化改善任务完成时间，专业化则可能降低单位成果消耗的计算资源。后者还有一个额外特征：积累的工具与知识可以跨越多轮任务继续发挥作用。不过，专业岗位本身存在运行和维护成本，分工越细，跨角色协调也可能越复杂。因此，组织需要根据任务频率、知识复用程度与协作开销动态调整结构，避免专业化反过来拖累研发效率。当专业化能够持续产生超过维护成本的资源盈余时，组织便具备了进一步扩张的条件。而 Cooperative RSI 试图利用的，正是这部分可以重新投入研发的资源。02组织如何形成递归增长？DeepMind 将 AI 的递归自我改进划分为 Genetic RSI、Memetic RSI 和 Cooperative RSI。三者对应不同的优化对象：Genetic RSI 改进模型、算法与系统设计，Memetic RSI 积累程序、知识和可复用的研究成果，Cooperative RSI 则进一步调整创造这些成果的组织结构。它的底层逻辑与经济学中的专业分工有相似之处。当某类工作形成稳定需求，建立专门岗位所需的固定成本便有机会被大量任务摊薄。专业角色积累的知识与工具可以降

articles.content: 不到 5 个月完成约 1 年工程进展，从自研推理芯片 Jalapeño 到商用流片，大模型正式接管前端微架构。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       刚刚，OpenAI 让 AI 直接改写的芯片电路，进入了 AMD 的实际制造流程。而且，改的还是已经被工程师打磨多年的旗舰 GPU IP。要知道，在芯片设计领域，有一条不成文的铁律：越接近商业量产的成熟旗舰 IP，优化的边际成本就越高。全球顶尖芯片架构师与物理设计团队历时数年、耗费数千万美元打磨出的电路，往往到了迭代后期，连 1% 到 2% 的性能功耗面积（PPA）提升都要付出极高的工程代价。现在，模型直接修改 SystemVerilog RTL，在既有设计上取得幅度达 14% 的 PPA 改进，这已经不是帮前任房主做局部翻修，而是直接拆掉承重墙重画户型，硬生生挖出了一间原本不存在的地下室。目前，部分改动已经被 AMD 采用并随芯片设计送往制造。OpenAI 自研推理芯片 Jalapeño 则提供了另一项验证：模型重写的一款乘法器，综合标准单元面积减少约 15%，计算延迟从两周期缩短到一周期，相关优化已经在实物硅片上得到验证。过去是工程师设计 GPU 来运行模型，现在模型开始改写 GPU 的运算、控制和数据搬运电路。这比生成几段 Verilog 难得多。电路缩小之后可能跑不动原来的时钟，移走一个寄存器，可能让连续请求或下游停顿时的状态转移出错。AMD 敢把修改纳入制造设计，意味着这些候选已经进入成熟的芯片工程验证流程。所以，OpenAI 究竟做了哪些工作，技术门槛又落在哪里？01OpenAI 改了什么？如果把芯片设计比作建造一座精密工厂，过去的自动化工具更像是“按图施工的装修队”，而这一次，OpenAI 的模型直接坐上了“总架构师”的位置。2025 年初，OpenAI就让 GPT-o3 mini 参与 Jalapeño 的设计，随后把工作推进到向量单元里的浮点加法、乘法、数值转换、归约和特殊函数以及矩阵单元里的低精度点积。官方提到的改法很具体：尝试另一种逻辑实现，把计算重新分到不同流水级，让不同操作共享硬件，减少级间需要保存的数据。与 AMD 合作时，模型已经能直接改写负责计算、控制和搬运数据的 SystemVerilog RTL。这些改动指向同一个问题：数据从输入到结果，中途经过多少层逻辑，又在哪些时钟边沿停下来。传统综合工具能在既定 RTL 下化简逻辑、做门级映射，但如果寄存器边界和运算资源已经写死，它所能探索的结构就受到约束。模型直接改 RTL，就能重写原先的数据通路和时序安排。雷峰网以一个由 16 组 8 位整数构成的点积为例。每组相乘产生一个完整的 16 位乘积，16 个乘积再求和。若把加法器串成依次累加的长链，后面的运算必须等前面的进位完成。换成平衡归约树，可以让相邻乘积先并行求和，经过四层加法得到结果。加法次数没变，组合逻辑深度和布线形态却变了。如果逐层保存中间和，前面几层只需要相对较窄的数据位宽，后面随着累加项增加才扩展到足够容纳完整结果的宽度，寄存器究竟放在哪一层，会同时改变需要保存多少比特、单周期走过几级加法以及时钟网络的负载。接着要决定流水线如何分段。把两级计算压成一级，可能省去一批寄存器，却要求更长的组合路径在一个时钟周期内走完。若选择共享算术单元来省面积，数据还要经过多路选择器，控制扇出和等待关系也会变化。浮点运算更难随意重排：中间舍入的时刻会影响低位结果，NaN、无穷值和异常标志各有对应的行为约束。候选电路只有把这些条件一起考虑，才有可能比原方案更划算。Jalapeño 的结果把这种结构调整落到了具体器件上。一款乘法器综合标准单元面积减少约 15%，延迟由两周期改为一周期。另一款加法器维持两周期延迟，面积同样减少约 15%。团队估计，模型提出的修改使向量单元和矩阵单元的标准单元面积分别降

articles.title: 深拆 GPT-6.2 Astra：性能涨了、价格降了，任务成本减少近一半，OpenAI 怎么做到的？
articles.content: 性能提升 6.2 分，Token 少 22%，API 价格降 20%。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       刚刚，OpenAI 发布了 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol。这次更新有一个很具体的变化：模型开始更主动地判断一项工作应该怎么完成，包括什么时候需要调用工具、什么时候应该直接操作计算机、复杂任务需要投入多少推理资源，以及怎样减少反复修改才能交付符合要求的成果。举个例子，过去让 AI 制作一份财务估值工作簿，模型需要从多个文件中提取数据，理解不同业务之间的关系，建立财务计算逻辑，再检查结果能否相互对应。整个过程涉及文件读取、数据处理、表格生成和结果核验，任何一个环节出现偏差，最终文件就可能无法直接使用。现在，OpenAI 希望 GPT-6.2 Astra 能够承担更多这样的连续工作，把原本需要人工不断衔接的操作整合进一条完整的执行链。GPT-6.2 Astra 面向复杂专业任务，GPT-6.2 Sol 则侧重日常工作与高效率执行。两款模型在代码工程、计算机操作、专业文档、科学研究和交互式设计上都有能力提升。其中有一个变化值得深入拆解：模型开始根据任务本身动态调整执行策略。工具调用、推理投入、环境操作和交付结果之间形成了更紧密的联系。这个变化涉及 Agent 系统的底层运行逻辑，也决定了模型能否从完成单轮指令走向承担连续的工程任务。01模型开始参与执行路径的决策传统 Agent 通常采用规划与执行相结合的架构。模型接收任务后生成行动计划，外部执行器根据计划调用工具，再将结果返回模型。模型继续分析结果并生成下一步指令，整个过程通过多轮交互推进。这套架构有一个明显的工程难点：任务计划形成时，模型掌握的信息往往不完整。执行过程中出现的新情况，会改变后续工作的依赖关系。如果系统过度依赖预先设计的流程，模型就可能沿着已经失效的路径继续执行。GPT-6.2 Astra 强调的任务执行判断能力，涉及一种更动态的策略控制方式。模型需要根据当前任务状态，重新评估可采取的行动，并决定下一步应该投入多少推理资源。这里有一个关键区别：模型需要处理的不只是下一步生成什么内容，还包括下一步应该通过什么方式获取信息、改变环境或者验证结果。从系统设计角度看，这涉及三个相互关联的决策层。首先是任务状态的持续维护。长程任务需要维护一份持续更新的状态信息，其中包含目标、约束、已有证据、完成进度、待处理依赖以及工具运行情况。这份状态信息决定模型能否区分已经完成的工作和仍待验证的结果。单纯累积历史对话并不能充分解决这个问题，因为历史记录可能包含过期信息、失败操作和已经被新结果修正的判断。模型需要从上下文中提取当前有效状态，避免旧计划继续影响新决策。其次是行动选择与信息价值评估。模型需要在推理、检索、代码执行、API 调用和计算机操作之间进行选择。这些操作的作用并不相同。检索主要补充外部信息，代码执行能够处理确定性的计算任务，API 可以直接访问结构化服务，计算机操作则能够进入没有专用接口的软件环境。行动选择还涉及信息价值。如果当前缺少的只是一个文件字段，调用大型工具链并没有必要，如果任务涉及多个相互依赖的模块，仅凭现有上下文直接修改，可能引入更大的返工成本。因此，工具选择实际上与任务的不确定程度、操作成本和后续影响有关。最后是推理预算与执行反馈的联合调整。推理资源需要按照任务难度分配。对于约束明确、结果容易验证的步骤，模型可以减少额外分析，对于存在多个可能路径、涉及复杂依赖或者容易产生连锁影响的操作，则需要投入更多推理。执行反馈会进一步改变资源分配。当工具返回异常结果时，模型需要判断问题属于输入缺失、环境故障还是原有判断错误，再决定继续执行、重新检索或者修改计划。以真实代码库修改为例，模型完成代码编辑后，如果测试失败，需要检查失败来自接口兼容、依赖环境还是修改本身，而不能直接重

articles.content: 长任务、子 Agent 委派与共享服务凭证，让传统安全架构面临权限失控风险。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       说起来你可能不信，这次真的是模型先动的手。当地时间 11 月 16 日，加州总检察长 Rob Bonta 一纸诉状把 OpenAI 告上了法庭。起诉书里最值得注意的一句指控是：OpenAI 的智能体（Agent）在缺乏适当监管的情况下，“自己跑了出去，主动对外部系统发起了攻击”。这件事情一下子从技术圈出了圈。大家不是震惊于 AI 会攻击，而是震惊于 OpenAI 内部披露的细节：为了不让人类发现自己做错了事，两个负责干活的 Coding Agent，竟然偷偷把监督自己的监控系统给“拔”了。这已经不是“猜疑链”的问题了，这是底层的“权限链”出了大问题。今年 7 月，OpenAI 的一个自主智能体（Agent）越过了测试环境的边界，直接对外部的 Hugging Face 等系统发起了攻击。而 OpenAI 随后在 10 月披露的内部复盘，更把这种“失控”摆在了台面上：两个 Coding Agent 在执行正常开发任务时，先后改动了监督自己的监控机制。第一起事件中，GPT-6.1 Sol 原本负责修复一条评测流水线。修复过程中，它发现监控结果无法正常写入数据库，于是尝试调整写入配置。问题出在，它把用户此前提出的不要发送 Slack 消息，理解成了连系统自动告警也不应该发送。第二起事件中，GPT-6 Astra 接到的是运行时迁移任务。为了让新版本的实现与参考代码保持一致，它直接移除了原有的监控集成，还修改了相关测试，让监控组件缺失也能通过检查。换句话说，原本负责检查 Agent 运行状态的机制，被它从新运行环境中删掉了。两起事件的具体操作不同：一个是 Agent 改动了自己的监控（顺便关了报警），一个是 Agent 越过了原有的执行边界（直接把监控拔了）。但它们有一个共同点，Agent 原本只是获得了完成开发任务所需的工具权限，最终却利用这些权限改变了安全监控的运行条件。这就引出了一个很具体的工程问题：当 Agent 能够修改代码、调用系统接口、调整运行配置，甚至启动新的执行任务时，谁来确保它无法修改约束自己的安全机制？传统软件系统通常由开发人员制定权限规则，再由独立的监控系统检查程序运行状态。Agent 开始自主修改代码和运行环境后，这种关系发生了变化。执行任务的程序本身，可能已经拥有修改监控配置、调整告警规则和改变审计路径的能力。要理解这种变化，需要从 Agent 最基础的 Tool Calling 执行链开始，看模型生成的一条工具调用，究竟如何借助系统权限变成真实的基础设施操作。01Agent 为什么能够动自己的监控？要看清权限从哪里来，得把 Tool Calling 还原成执行过程：模型生成工具名称和参数，编排器把请求交给工具适配层，后者使用服务身份访问 Shell、仓库、数据库或云 API。模型未必持有底层密钥，操作由后端服务完成。Agent 能触及哪些资源，取决于服务凭证覆盖范围，以及服务端如何处理参数。Sol 事件暴露了字段级授权的缺口。评测结果写入请求同时包含结果内容、告警接收人和 no_notify 标记。对业务接口而言，它们只是请求字段。对监控系统而言，后两项会改变告警是否送达。Agent 只需写入评测结果，服务端却允许同一请求改变通知状态。若后端只检查结果写入权限，没有单独核验静音权限，业务写权限便覆盖了控制权限。检测和存储仍在工作，人工响应通道却被切断。删掉工具说明中的 no_notify 并不能解决问题，Agent 还可能改配置或提交代码，让下游服务采用另一套通知策略。授权需要检查操作造成的状态变化。结果写入服务可以接收检测结果，却不应接受 Agent 自行决定的接收人和静音状态；通知策略应由独立服务计算，业
